questions: I'm new, where do I begin?
answers.answer:
Duracash makes sure finished work gets billed with everything the payer needs, then follows the money until it's paid.
- Create a job with the contract amount, payer, approver, AP email and retainage percent.
- Put the paperwork on the job record: drop photos and PDFs, or bring in emails, texts and notes through the Inbox.
- Record progress. Duracash drafts the pay app, withholds retainage and lists the packet the payer requires.
- Attach records to the packet. Approve and send unlocks when nothing is missing.
- Match the payment, send the waiver, finish the punch list, collect retainage, close the job.
follow_ups: How do I create a job?
How do I import emails and texts?

questions: How do I create a job?
How do I add a new job?
Where do I enter a contract?
answers.answer: Go to Jobs and click New job. Required: job name, address, customer, approver, AP email and the contract amount. Set the retainage percent if the contract holds retainage, and pick the role: Owner if you bill the property owner or homeowner, GC if you are a sub billing a general contractor. The customer's details become its payer playbook.

questions: How do I edit a job?
I made a typo in the job name
How do I delete a job?
Can I change the contract amount?
answers.answer: Editing or deleting a job isn't built yet; it is on the next build list. For now, add a note to the job record with the correction. A payer's approver, AP email and packet rules can be changed in the Payer Playbook.

questions: What does the role field mean?
What is the role on a new job?
answers.answer: Role says who pays you. Owner: you bill the property owner or homeowner directly. GC: you are a subcontractor billing a general contractor. GC jobs usually need a schedule of values, insurance certificate and waivers with every pay app.

questions: Can I use this on my phone?
answers.answer: There's no separate app yet. Duracash runs in your phone's browser: sign in at the same address. On a phone, Choose files opens the camera, so you can photograph tickets straight into the Inbox or a job.
follow_ups: How do I import emails and texts?

questions: Can I add my office manager?
How do I invite my bookkeeper?
Can more than one person log in?
answers.answer: Yes. An owner opens Team & account and invites people by email, as owner or member. Members do the everyday work (jobs, pay apps, sends); owners also manage the team, the inbound addresses, reset and deleting the company. Every action shows in the Audit with the person's name. If email isn't set up on the server, the owner gets an invite link to pass on; it works once, for 7 days.

questions: What's the difference between a pay app and an invoice?
Can I get a PDF of the pay app?
answers.answer: A pay app (pay application) is the bill for work done this period. It lists what was completed, line by line if the job has a schedule of values, adds signed change orders, and subtracts retainage. Many contracts also require a packet of paperwork with it. Open any pay app to download it as a PDF; the same PDF goes with the email when you send it.
follow_ups: What is a packet?
What is retainage?

questions: How do I bill progress on a job?
How do I make a progress pay app?
Bill for work done this month
answers.answer: Open the job and click Progress pay app. With a schedule of values, enter how much of each line is done to date; without one, enter the completed-to-date dollar amount (the total done so far, not just this month). Duracash drafts a pay app for the difference since the last one, withholds retainage, and builds the packet from the payer's playbook. The job stays in progress.
follow_ups: What is a packet?
What is a pencil copy?

questions: How do I mark a job done?
The job is finished, what now?
answers.answer: Open the job, click Mark done, add completion notes and confirm. Duracash drafts the final pay app for everything not billed yet. If a draft is already open, send or void it first; the message names it. Jobs with retainage get a closeout packet for the punch list.
follow_ups: How do I get retainage released?

questions: How do I send a pay app?
answers.answer: Open the job and click Approve & send. It stays off while the packet is missing something or an unsigned change order is on the pay app; the red box lists what's missing. When email is set up, the pay app goes to the payer's AP email with the packet documents attached, from your company name, and replies come back to you. The Outbox shows whether it was delivered.
follow_ups: What is a packet?
Did the customer get my pay app?

questions: How do I send a pencil draft?
Can the GC review before I submit?
answers.answer: A pencil copy is the draft pay app sent to the owner or GC to agree quantities and change orders before the formal one, so nothing gets pushed to next month. With a draft open, click Send pencil copy on the job. When they answer, click Payer agreed to pencil or Payer wants changes and note what they said.
follow_ups: How do I send a pay app?

questions: How do I delete a draft pay app?
answers.answer: Open the job and click Void draft. The draft is kept in history as void and its work goes back to unbilled, so you can draft again. A pay app that was already sent can't be voided in Duracash.

questions: Why can't I draft a pay app?
answers.answer: Nothing to draft means all completed work is already on a pay app. Record more progress (completed-to-date) or mark the job done first. If a draft is already open, Duracash says so and names it.

questions: What is a schedule of values?
Line items on a pay app
Can I bill by quantity and unit rate?
How do I set up a schedule of values?
Bill by quantities and unit rates
Import my schedule of values from Excel
answers.answer: A schedule of values breaks the contract into lines: a quantity at a unit rate (or a lump sum), with overhead and profit on top. Open the job and click Set up schedule of values, before the first pay app. Paste rows straight from Excel, Google Sheets, a CSV or your estimate PDF, or type them; the total has to equal the contract. Each progress pay app then asks how much of each line is done to date and bills the difference line by line, like an AIA G703 continuation sheet. Approved change orders add their own lines.

questions: Why does a pay app need a packet?
answers.answer: The packet is everything the contract says must go with a pay app: lien waivers, delivery tickets, photos, signed change orders, schedule of values, insurance certificate. Duracash lists the items from the payer's playbook and won't let the pay app go out until each one is in.
follow_ups: How do I clear a packet item?
How do I change what a payer requires?

questions: How do I clear a packet item?
How do I mark something present?
How do I attach a document to the packet?
answers.answer: Open the pay app's packet. For each item, either pick a record from the job record and click Attach from job record, or click Mark present and say why (for example "emailed to the GC on 10/12"). A reason or an attached record is required, so the audit shows how each item was satisfied.
follow_ups: How do I import emails and texts?

questions: How do I change what a payer requires?
answers.answer: The Payer Playbook keeps each payer's rules: approver, AP email, follow-up days, usual approval days, packet items, and why they've rejected pay apps before. Packet items are separated by commas; new pay apps use the list. Teach playbook on a blocked job adds a rejection reason.

questions: How do I add a change order?
Extra work the customer asked for
answers.answer: Add a change order from Change Orders (or the job's Add change order button) with a title and amount. It's pending until the customer signs: then click Approve and it's billable. Approved after the job is done? It still becomes billable on the next pay app.
follow_ups: Can I bill an unsigned change order?
The customer won't sign the change order

questions: Can I bill an unsigned change order?
Put a change order on the pay app before it's signed
Can I bill a change order that isn't signed yet?
Change order not signed, can I bill it?
answers.answer: You can put a pending change order on the next pay app (Put on next pay app), so the dollars are on the draft. Approve & send stays blocked until it's signed, so an unsigned CO never goes out by accident.

questions: The customer won't sign the change order
answers.answer: Click Withdraw on the pending change order. If it's on an open draft, void the draft first, then withdraw it and draft again. A withdrawn change order stays in history.

questions: How do I record a payment?
The customer paid, what do I do?
answers.answer: Open the job, click Match payment, pick the pay app it's for, enter the amount and the check number or QuickBooks reference. A partial payment stays partial. Paid in full opens the waiver for that pay app. The amount can't be more than what's owed, and a reference can only be used once per job.
follow_ups: What is a lien waiver?
Does it connect to QuickBooks?

questions: They only paid part of it
They paid only part of the pay app
Customer paid less than the bill
answers.answer: Record what came in. The pay app shows as partial with the rest still outstanding, and no waiver is due until it's paid in full. Follow up on the balance from Collections.

questions: Why do I need a waiver?
answers.answer: A lien waiver gives up your lien rights for money you've been paid. Conditional: it only takes effect if the payment clears. Unconditional: payment received. Some states require exact statutory forms, so use the form your state or the payer requires; Duracash doesn't generate it.
follow_ups: How do I send a waiver?

questions: How do I send a waiver?
answers.answer: When a pay app is paid in full, the job shows Send waiver. Drop your signed waiver on the job record first (kind: lien waiver): the email attaches the newest one not sent before; with none, it tells the payer the waiver follows. One waiver per paid pay app, and never before the payment is matched. Duracash doesn't write waiver forms; states set them.
Retainage is a percentage (often 5 to 10) the payer keeps from every pay app until the job is closed out. Duracash withholds it on each pay app, shows it as a line, and tracks it until it's released.
follow_ups: How do I get retainage released?
Which jobs are holding my retainage?

questions: How do I get retainage released?
How do I ask for retainage?
How do I get my retainage back?
How do I get retainage paid?
When do I get my retainage?
answers.answer: Retainage is released at closeout. A job with retainage gets a closeout packet (punch list signoff and whatever the payer's playbook lists). Finish those items, mark the job done, then click Chase retainage to ask for release. When the money arrives, click Record retainage paid.

Each payer has follow-up days in its playbook. A follow-up on a sent pay app is allowed once that many days have passed since it was sent (or since the last follow-up). If you try earlier, Duracash tells you the date it's due. Each follow-up is emailed to the payer's AP contact and listed in the Outbox.

questions: Where do I see unpaid pay apps?
answers.answer: Collections lists every job with money outstanding, how many days since it was sent, who to contact, and buttons to follow up, email or call.

questions: Did the customer get my pay app?
Where do I see what I sent?
Who does the email come from?
answers.answer: The Outbox lists every approved email and what happened to it: sent (with the time), failed (with the reason, such as an address the payer's mail server refused), or not sent. A failed or unsent email has a Send again button. Pay apps go out with the packet documents attached, from "your company via Duracash", and the payer's reply goes to whoever approved the send. The demo account never sends real email.
No. Automated calls to customers need prior consent under federal law and are not planned before a lawyer reviews it. Collections has a Call button that opens your phone.

questions: How do I import emails and texts?
How do I upload a document?
Can I bring in my paperwork?
How do I upload a file?
How do I upload a pdf or photo?
answers.answer:
Three ways:
- Drop files anywhere (photos, PDFs, Word, Excel, CSV, saved emails). On a job page they go straight onto that job; elsewhere they land in the Inbox.
- Paste an email, a text thread or your notes in the Inbox.
- Forward email and texts automatically once an email service and a Twilio number are connected (Inbox, Bring emails and texts in automatically).
The Inbox suggests the job from the job code, address, job name or sender; you file with one click.
follow_ups: How do I import 30 days of notes?
How does it know which job?

questions: How do I import 30 days of notes?
answers.answer: Copy the notes and paste them in the Inbox with "Notes: one daily record per date" selected. Start each day with a date (10/12, Oct 12, or 2026-10-12). Duracash splits them into one daily record per date and keeps the original date when you file them.

questions: How does it know which job?
Why didn't it suggest a job?
answers.answer: It looks for the job code (like OAK), the job address, the job name, the customer's name, or an email from the payer's AP address. If two jobs fit equally, it asks you to pick. Tip: put the job code in email subjects and texts. You can always change the job before filing, and Undo takes a filed item back off.

questions: How do I forward emails to Duracash?
answers.answer: Automatic email needs an email service that posts incoming mail to a web address (SendGrid, Mailgun or Postmark); automatic texts need a Twilio number. The Inbox shows the private addresses to paste into those services. Until they're connected, save emails as .eml or paste them, and paste or screenshot texts.

questions: What file types can I upload?
answers.answer: PDF, JPG, PNG, GIF, WEBP, HEIC, Word (.doc, .docx), Excel (.xls, .xlsx), CSV, TXT and saved emails (.eml), up to 15 MB each. Drop the file on any page (on a job page it goes straight onto that job), or use Choose files in the Inbox. Web pages and SVG files are refused for safety.

questions: How do I log what happened today?
answers.answer: A daily record is a dated note of what happened on site: crew, work done, deliveries, problems. Add one in Daily Record, or paste many at once in the Inbox as notes. They live on the job record and can be attached to a packet as backup.
The calendar shows work complete, pay apps sent, follow-ups due, expected approvals, payments, waivers and closeouts. Pick a job in the filter to see only that job. Click a day for its events.
follow_ups: Can I put this on Google Calendar?

questions: Can I put this on Google Calendar?
answers.answer: Yes. In Calendar, open "Put these dates on your phone", copy the private address, and in Google Calendar on a computer choose Other calendars, +, From URL. Apple Calendar and Outlook can subscribe to the same address. Calendar apps refresh it on their own schedule, often every few hours.

questions: When do I have to file a lien?
answers.answer: Not yet. Lien and notice deadlines depend on the state, your role and the project type, and a wrong date can cost lien rights, so Duracash won't calculate them until they're reviewed by a lawyer for a specific state. The calendar shows billing dates only.

questions: How do I export my data?
Can I get my data out?
answers.answer: Click Export data in the left rail. It downloads your company's data as a file. Keep a copy if you want your own backup.

Reset deletes every job, payer and record in your company. To confirm, you type your company name exactly; a snapshot is kept on the server first. On the demo account, reset puts the sample data back.

On the sign-in screen, click Forgot your password? and enter your email: a reset link arrives that works once, for one hour, and signs you out everywhere else. Signed in, change it on Team & account. After 5 wrong passwords for one email, sign-in pauses for 15 minutes. Passwords need at least 10 characters. If the server can't send email yet, the screen says so; ask the Duracash team.

Each company's data is kept separate; only your team's logins can see it, and owners decide who is on the team. Passwords are stored as one-way hashes; reset links work once and expire. Duracash is still early: keep your own copies of signed documents, and use Export data for a copy. Questions you ask here are saved so the team can add better answers.
This helper answers from a library of prepared answers and your own job data; it isn't an AI model. When AI features arrive, you'll approve everything they send.

Not yet. A read-only QuickBooks Online import of customers, invoices and payments is planned. Today you record payments by hand with Match payment, and you can drop exported QuickBooks reports (CSV, PDF) into the Inbox.
There are no direct connections to other software yet. Duracash sits beside the tools you use: export reports, photos or PDFs from them and drop the files into the Inbox.

Billing isn't live, so nothing is charged today. The trial is timed to the payment cycle: nothing to pay until the first pay app you send through Duracash is paid, or 90 days, whichever comes first (120 if a pay app is still unpaid at day 90). Your dashboard shows where your trial stands.

questions: I need help from a human
answers.answer: Contact the Duracash founders directly by email for now. Tell them what you clicked and what you expected; a screenshot helps. Questions you ask here are saved, so they also see what's missing.

The dashboard shows billed this month, finished-but-unbilled work, outstanding, retainage held, blocked jobs and active jobs, then what needs action and every open job. Hover a label and click its (i) for what it means.

A status always names what's holding the job up, for example "Conditional lien waiver is missing" or "Submitted to Ellison, awaiting Dev Patel". It never just says pending. The next column says what to do.
Audit lists every action: when, who (the signed-in person), and what changed. Filter by job.

questions: What are the little i icons?
answers.answer: Hover any label, column or tile: a small (i) appears next to it. Hover or tap the (i) to see what that field means. The Help page has the full glossary.

questions: How do I close a job?
Why can't I close this job?
answers.answer: Close for record appears when work is done and nothing is left: no open draft, no pending change order, nothing unbilled or unpaid, retainage released and waivers sent. Until then the job page lists exactly what's left. Closed jobs move to Job history and become read-only.

questions: How do I delete my account?
answers.answer: An owner can delete the company on Team & account: type your password and the company name. It removes every job, file, payer and record, and every user on the team, at once. Use Export data first if you want a copy. Server backups that already hold the data expire on their own (the newest 14 are kept by default).
follow_ups: How do I export my data?

questions: Do you back up my data?
What if the server loses my data?
answers.answer: Yes. The server makes a backup every 24 hours (and on start-up when the last one is older) and keeps the newest 14. They sit on the same server as your data, so they guard against mistakes and bugs, not against losing the server itself. Keep your own copy with Export data, and keep signed documents outside Duracash too.
follow_ups: How do I export my data?

questions: Why do I need to confirm my email?
I didn't get the confirmation email
My emails say verify your email first
answers.answer: Duracash sends pay apps with replies coming back to the person who approved them, so it checks that the address is really yours first. Click the link in the confirmation email (it works for 3 days). Didn't get it? Use Send the link again on Team & account, then check spam. Emails held while you were unconfirmed have Send again in the Outbox.

questions: Where are the terms of service?
What do you do with my data?
answers.answer: The Terms of Service and the Privacy Policy are linked at the bottom of the sign-in page (/terms and /privacy). In short: your data is yours, we use it only to run Duracash for you, we don't sell it or use it for advertising, the app loads no tracking scripts, and an owner can export or delete everything. Both pages say if they are still a draft awaiting a lawyer's review.
follow_ups: Is my data safe?
